requirement: A site's dump is imported only into the database server its first boot keeps, on provision and on restore

oracle.ref: PR #893 (fix); fix evidence: 05/10/2026 local stand: 1 of ~40 WordPress site creations (run initb-0510-wpx-v1) failed at 'importing database' with ERROR 2002 "Can't connect to local server through socket '/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock'" right after 'starting database' had passed its SELECT 1; docker logs of the db showed 'Creating database wordpress' and 'Stopping temporary server' in the same second (ledger L13). Red 65b7fa609 (6 of 7 cases not ok on 16063e8f8), fix de8adf7f4.
oracle.invariant: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 8). Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): the wait answers ready only when the server says skip_networking is off through the import's own client and socket; a refusing server is waited for, a server that never answers or stays the temporary one stops the run with the last refusal before any import, a password the volume does not know is named, and restore drops the database and pours the dump only on the server that stays up, stopping before DROP DATABASE when it never answers.
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command

writes: run dir under QA_ARTIFACT_ROOT: logs/, tmp/<case> (the child TMPDIR, removed after the run)

assertionIds: provision: the import never lands in the gap between the first boot temporary server and the real one
provision: a database that refuses its first connections is waited for, then imported into
provision: a database that never answers stops the run with the last refusal, before any import
provision: a server that stays the temporary one is never taken for ready
provision: a password the volume does not know is named as the reason
restore: the database is dropped and the dump poured in only on the server that stays up
restore: a database that never answers stops before DROP DATABASE
